title: Chicken Thighs Saltimbocca – Braised
description: We love all things “saltimbocca” – meaning “jump into your mouth!” In this variation, using chicken rather than veal, we also make this with an easy braising approach. This means that it can be scaled up fairly easily, like we did for the Family Reunion 2022 in North Myrtle Beach. “Life is Delicious. Savor it.”
ingredients: 4 oz sliced Prosciutto thinly sliced or torn up (or pancetta or bacon)
2 lbs chicken thighs (preferably with skin on and bones)
4 (or more) sage leaves, thinly sliced or chopped
directions: Clean any excessive fat off the thighs, and season with salt and pepper.
Heat a sauté pan over medium high heat.

Add a little olive oil to the pan, and sear the thighs on both sides until brown (about 8 minutes with skin side down first, then 3-4 minutes after turning). Remove the thighs to a plate, and reserve.

Add the shallots to the pan and cook until softened and lightly colored, about 2 minutes. (If you’re using uncooked pancetta or bacon, add those in with the shallots). Add garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Deglaze with wine and lemon juice, scraping up any browned bits.
Add the prosciutto to the pan with the juices, and sauté for 1-2 minutes.
Add the thighs, sage, 1 cup of hot or boiling chicken stock, and then simmer (or baked in a 350 degree oven) until the thighs are cooked through, about 15 minutes.

Remove the pan from the heat and take out the thighs for a moment. Sprinkle the sauce with a little cornstarch or flour or Wondra, and whisk in some butter. Season to taste with salt and pepper, possibly stirring in more lemon juice, and generous sprinkling of Parmesan.
Put the thighs back in the sauce, and toss to coat.
Serve with some buttered noodles, or polenta, or mashed potatoes, or something to soak up more of the heavenly sauce – jumping into your mouth on the way to Heaven!
